chunks: From it, regarding the state of the people of the graves on the Day of Resurrection:
They have fixed their gaze from the resting places of the graves, and have gone to the final destinations; for every house its own people, they do not exchange it nor are they moved from it.
And commanding good and forbidding evil are two characteristics of Allah, the Glorified, and indeed they do not bring near the appointed time, nor do they decrease sustenance.
ai.seo_question: What is the effect of commanding good and forbidding evil on a person's lifespan and sustenance?
ai.summary: In this passage from the 'Malice borne by Aisha' chapter, Imam Ali describes the fixed state of souls in their graves (Barzakh) on the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing the permanence of their abode. He elevates *Amr bil-Ma'ruf wa Nahy anil-Munkar* (Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil) to a divine attribute (*Khuluq Allah*), clarifying that these duties are intrinsic to God's nature and do not diminish one's lifespan (*Ajal*) or provision (*Rizq*), countering common superstitions.
